notes.note: Paul's rule: every new layer joins on probation. Good, and I'd like the same treatment. Clutter never announces itself; it arrives one helpful layer at a time. Each should earn its seat.
Paul adds a guardian per breath: the Nutcracker, Balanchine, a bard. 'If this is too many it's ok.' It is too many, says the guardian with fifty opinions about glass.
Paul struck Paper Lantern as a near-duplicate of Lantern Paper, and he was right. Two names for one color is clutter in a nice coat.
Paul wants the palette released a few colors at a time. Thirty-six swatches at once is a shouting match; a slow reveal is quiet chrome that lets each color be seen.
Paul said tone the Georgian down, gently. Right. A bold brand needs one bright accent, not a neon sign on every screen. Let the glass carry it quietly.
Paul's leap is a coloring book with footnotes, which I approve of, having a few myself. Keep the margin for words and the page for paint.

favorite_idea.why: A palette that arrives a few colors at a time is quiet chrome in motion, and it stops thirty-six colors from shouting at once.

steer: Keep each aside short and let the plain sentences carry Paul's credit, so the chapter feels as calm as the app it describes.
